purpose: P0-S2 evidence batch 3: KR-study, KR-work, CN-study, CN-work, IT-work, RU-study, RU-work.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in South Korea must obtain a D-2 student visa. Applicants must hold a valid acceptance letter from a recognised Korean higher-education institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means, and satisfy the general conditions for entry under Korean immigration law administered by the Korea Immigration Service.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service guidance for D-2 student visa.

records.claim: South Korea requires D-2 student visa applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover tuition and living costs. Applicants must provide evidence of financial support such as bank statements or a sponsor's financial guarantee; the applicable threshold is assessed by the Korean consulate in the applicant's country of residence.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service financial-means requirements for D-2 student visa.

records.claim: D-2 student visa applications are submitted at the Korean consulate or embassy in the applicant's country of residence. After arrival, the applicant must register with the Korea Immigration Service within 90 days. The visa is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be extended annually.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service application process for D-2 student visa.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in South Korea must obtain the appropriate employment visa category. The E-7 Specially Designated Activities visa covers professional and technical roles; applicants must have a confirmed job offer from a Korean employer and meet the qualification and experience requirements for the designated occupation.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service guidance for employment visa categories.

records.claim: South Korea's employment visa categories require the applicant to receive remuneration in accordance with the applicable Korean minimum wage or the sector-specific rate for the role. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Korean labour law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service financial requirements for employment visas.

records.claim: Employment visa applications for South Korea are submitted at the Korean consulate or embassy in the applicant's country of residence. The employer must obtain a confirmation of visa issuance from the Korea Immigration Service before the applicant applies. After arrival, the applicant must register with the Korea Immigration Service.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Korea Immigration Service application process for employment visas.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in China must obtain an X1 or X2 student visa. X1 is for study programmes of more than 180 days; X2 is for 180 days or less. Applicants must hold a valid JW201 or JW202 admission form from a Chinese educational institution and satisfy the general conditions for entry under Chinese immigration law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China guidance for student visa categories.

records.claim: China requires student visa applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover tuition and living costs. Applicants must provide evidence of financial support such as bank statements or a scholarship award letter; the applicable threshold is assessed by the Chinese consulate in the applicant's country of residence.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China financial-means requirements for student visas.

records.claim: Chinese student visa applications are submitted at the Chinese consulate or embassy in the applicant's country of residence. After arrival, X1 visa holders must apply for a Residence Permit within 30 days at the local public security bureau. The residence permit is issued for the duration of the study programme.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China application process for student visas.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in China must obtain a Z work visa and a Work Permit for Foreigners. Applicants must have a confirmed job offer from a Chinese employer authorised to hire foreign nationals. The employer must obtain the work permit before the applicant applies for the Z visa.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China guidance for work visa and permit.

records.claim: China's work visa and permit require the applicant to receive remuneration in accordance with the applicable Chinese minimum wage or the sector-specific rate for the role. The salary must be specified in the employment contract and comply with Chinese labour law.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China financial requirements for work visa.

records.claim: Chinese work visa applications require the employer to first obtain a Work Permit for Foreigners from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security. The applicant then applies for a Z visa at the Chinese consulate or embassy. After arrival, the applicant must apply for a Residence Permit within 30 days at the local public security bureau.
records.methodology: Direct review of current National Immigration Administration of China application process for work visa.

records.claim: Italy's work authorisation routes for third-country nationals operate within the annual Flussi quota decree. Non-seasonal subordinate work, self-employment and highly-qualified worker routes each have distinct eligibility criteria. The umbrella IT-work pathway record covers the family of routes; individual sub-routes (e.g. 2026 Flussi non-seasonal subordinate) have separate exact-route candidate records.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa guidance for work authorisation routes.

records.claim: Italy's work authorisation routes require the applicant to receive remuneration in accordance with the applicable national collective labour agreement (CCNL) for the role and sector. No single universal salary threshold applies across all work routes; the applicable rate is determined by the CCNL for the specific occupation and employer.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs work visa financial requirements. No unsupported universal salary figure is asserted.

records.claim: Italy's work authorisation routes require the employer to obtain a nulla osta (work authorisation) from the relevant Italian authority before the applicant applies for a work visa at the Italian consulate in their country of residence. The specific process varies by route (Flussi quota, EU Blue Card, intra-company transfer); applicants must follow the process for their specific route.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs work visa application process.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Russia must obtain a student visa. Applicants must hold a valid invitation letter from a recognised Russian educational institution and satisfy the general conditions for entry under Russian immigration law. Travel advisories and sanctions may affect the practical availability of this route for applicants from certain countries.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs student visa guidance. Confidence is medium due to geopolitical context and potential access restrictions.

records.claim: Russia requires student visa applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover living costs and tuition. The applicable threshold is assessed by the Russian consulate; no single universal figure is published. Practical access to banking and financial transfers may be restricted for applicants from certain countries due to sanctions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs student visa financial requirements. Confidence is medium due to geopolitical context.

records.claim: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Russia must obtain a work visa and work permit. The employer must obtain a work permit quota allocation and an individual work permit before the applicant applies for a work visa. Highly-qualified specialists may apply under a separate HQS route with different criteria. Travel advisories and sanctions may affect the practical availability of this route.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs work visa guidance. Confidence is medium due to geopolitical context.

records.claim: Russia's work visa requires the applicant to receive remuneration in accordance with the applicable Russian minimum wage or the HQS salary threshold for highly-qualified specialists. Practical access to banking and financial transfers may be restricted for applicants from certain countries due to sanctions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs work visa financial requirements. Confidence is medium due to geopolitical context.
